name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: I’ll pull Eitan’s latest design picks into a local folder for direct inspection—`mkdir -p ~/mine-ai-look/design-picks && cd ~/mine-ai-look/design-picks && curl -O https://mineai.com/eitan/picks.json && curl -O https://mineai.com/eitan/picks.zip && unzip -l picks.zip | wc -l` files listed. Then I’ll open the JSON and first 10 thumbnails in Preview to taste-test and log my reactions in `~/mine-ai-look/notes.md`.

name: Squint
text: Squint: Hold on—you’re assuming Eitan’s picks are *static* and *complete*, but the `unzip -l` count only tells us how many files are in the zip, not whether they’re the *latest* or *representative* of his current taste. What’s the timestamp on `picks.zip`? And have you verified that the JSON and ZIP are byte-for-byte identical to what’s live on the site? Without a checksum or `curl -I` headers, we’re trusting a black box.
